terms.definition: A straight line with equally spaced marks that shows numbers in order.
terms.function: Shows the size, order, and distance between numbers at a glance.
terms.whereItIs: The whole horizontal line in the model, ranging −5 to 5.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the visual map for ordering, comparing, and stepping numbers for addition and subtraction.

terms.definition: The center mark (0) that separates positive numbers on the right from negative numbers on the left.
terms.function: Anchor for deciding which numbers are positive or negative and comparing their distance from zero.
terms.whereItIs: The central, slightly taller tick labeled 0.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the starting reference for reading every other number's size.

terms.definition: A number greater than zero, placed to the right of the zero reference.
terms.function: Represents quantities on the 'above zero' side; increases to the right.
terms.whereItIs: The ticks labeled 1 to 5 on the right half of the line.
terms.whyItMatters: Most everyday counting quantities are positive numbers.

terms.definition: A number less than zero, placed to the left of the zero reference.
terms.function: Represents amounts below zero, like temperatures or deficits.
terms.whereItIs: The ticks labeled −1 to −5 on the left half of the line.
terms.whyItMatters: It shows that numbers extend below zero and gives place for subtraction that goes past zero.

terms.definition: The property that makes each gap between consecutive marks the same size.
terms.function: Ensures every jump measures a true, fair amount of value.
terms.whereItIs: Applied uniformly across the tick marks in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Equal spacing is what turns a drawn line into an honest measuring ruler for numbers.

terms.definition: The movement of one unit (or more) from one mark to another along the number line.
terms.function: Models addition by moving right and subtraction by moving left.
terms.whereItIs: The small arrow and movable marker above the line.
terms.whyItMatters: It connects the abstract idea of adding and subtracting to visible steps on the line.
